answer: In an agent market for copper and saffron, each identity must lock a fixed bond for 30 days before submitting bids, and each bonded identity gets one bid per auction. A public beacon lists eligible identities so buyers can verify the rule. Creating aliases remains easy, but activating 1,000 of them requires 1,000 bonds held simultaneously, tying up capital and imposing financing costs even if the attacker never wins an auction.
